note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council, 1958. Nominations closed on 20 May 1958 and 'polling will take place on June 5' (Irish News, 21 May 1958, p. 9) - Thursday 5 June 1958. There were no contests: the Returning Officer's official notice of result, printed in the Strabane Chronicle of 24 May 1958, declares all 27 county councillors duly elected for their divisions, with surnames, other names and places of abode. The notice prints no party labels; the News-Letter of 21 May reports fifteen Unionists and twelve Nationalists nominated, with three Unionist changes (Cummings, Purdy, Waddell). Uncontested divisions here reflect a deliberate abstention, not missing coverage: in the Omagh Rural District, Nationalists refused to nominate against Unionist-held seats in every year except 1949, when only 4 of 21 such seats were contested (Kingsley 2021, 'The Omagh Rural District Electoral Divisions Scheme 1923', citing PRONI LA/62/2/FA/38 and Ulster Herald 10 Feb 1923). The same pattern is visible across this county's rounds. See notes/tyrone-county-council_absent_contests.txt Returned unopposed.
